## The Kern Overnight
A truck fire that tipped over and burned down a trailer west of Bakersfield escalated into a wildland response around 9:47 p.m., drawing multiple engines, a dozer, helicopter 409 and a water tender. Crews worked to access the burn after the reporting party pointed out lights on the hill. Just before 3:45 a.m., a 53-foot trailer north of Pond on Garzoli Road was fully involved, with a spot of grass fire spreading alongside it. Battalion crews responded to what dispatch dubbed the Garzoli Incident and remained on scene for hotspots. Just before 10:45 p.m., a caller reported about 30 shots fired, mostly in a field in the area of Panama Lane & South Allen Road. The call stood for service while units investigated. Around 3:06 a.m., a welfare check near the Wells Fargo on Columbus Street escalated — a man on a bicycle was approached by subjects and an impact sound was heard, followed by a fight involving three people. Two suspects fled northbound Columbus; units searched. Just after 4 a.m., a big-rig incident with a load of table grapes brought a roadway closure in Delano, with Environmental Health notified.

## Today's weather
Expect a high near 98° and a low around 73° tonight. It's currently 95° at Meadows Field (KBFL). A Lake Wind Advisory is in effect until 11:00 p.m. tonight. Air quality is 112 — unhealthy for sensitive groups.

## Top stories
**KGET 17 reports that** the Trump administration's push to rescind protection on forested areas could have Kern County impact. **KGET 17 said that** the Shafter City Council will discuss a proposed ordinance banning sleeping in public places. **23ABC tells us that** a 21-year-old woman was arrested in a deadly South Bakersfield stabbing. Officers responded to a home in the 400 block of White Lane around 3:30 p.m. Monday, where they found a man who had been stabbed. He was pronounced dead at the scene. Homicide detectives investigated and arrested Erionna Russel, 21, on suspicion of second-degree murder. Police say Russel and the victim knew each other. Russel is scheduled to appear in court Wednesday afternoon. The victim's identity has not yet been released. **KGET 17 announced that** a California City man was arrested after the seizure of hundreds of pounds of narcotics and a firearm. **23ABC said that** California is holding firm on school vaccine rules as national rates dip. New CDC data shows kindergarten vaccination rates are slipping across the country, raising questions about how many children are starting school without all of their required shots. National vaccination coverage among kindergarteners fell by 0.1% for all reported vaccines during the 2025-26 school year. At the same time, exemptions from one or more vaccines rose to 4.2%, up from 3.6% the year before. The CDC says about 280,000 kindergarteners nationwide went into the 2025-26 school year without documentation of completing the MMR series. The report follows Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s visit to Kern County, where he described vaccine hesitancy as part of a broader crisis of public trust. "If the public does not trust the public health agencies, we are not going to have public health," Kennedy said. The latest CDC data show California's kindergarten MMR rate at 95.7%. According to the state's 2024-25 data, Kern County's overall immunization rate was 85.4%, which included virtual schools. When looking at classroom-based schools, that rate rises to 93.7%, similar to the state average. Kern Public Health says virtual schools may be exempt from immunization requirements. California law requires children entering TK through 12th grade to have documentation of required vaccinations. Unlike many states, California does not allow religious or personal-belief exemptions. Some students can still be admitted conditionally while they complete their vaccine series. Schools are required to follow up with families, and if a child does not come into compliance, they may be excluded from school. **23ABC announced that** the fight to save the Crystal Palace in Bakersfield continues. Buck Owens' Crystal Palace closed about a year ago, and its future remains uncertain. Now, one offer on the table would mean tearing it down. Country singer Scotty Crabtree started visiting the Palace in 1999. He says performing with its house band years later helped launch his career. "Basically, my professional career started in 2007 through getting to perform with the house band at the Crystal Palace," Crabtree said. Buck Owens opened the Crystal Palace in 1996, creating a home for the Bakersfield Sound. When Crabtree learned one offer could lead to demolition, he says he couldn't sit back and watch the Palace disappear. He started an online petition that has now gathered more than 200 signatures. The Buck Owens Private Foundation confirms it has received several offers — including one still on the table that would tear the building down. In a written statement, foundation representative Jim Shaw said the hope is to find a buyer who will reopen and reimagine the venue. "Since the listing and closing of the Crystal Palace last year we've had quite a bit of interest and several offers (including one still on the table that would be a tear-down!!). Our hope is that sooner rather than later the right person will step forward with a plan to reopen the venue in a manner that will bring our beautiful building back to life. Although in our perfect world the theme would remain Buck and the Bakersfield Sound, we accept that the new iteration might not resemble the version that we all remember. There are numerous ways that the venue could be reimagined, and we are open to all serious offers." **Bakersfield Now announced that** a DUI checkpoint & saturation patrol in Bakersfield ended in two arrests and seven citations.

## Something good
Bakersfield residents are pushing for more trees and cleaner air as heat and pollution concerns grow. This community effort highlights a proactive approach to improving local environmental conditions.
